blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Calibration of language models – the alignment between expressed or implicit confidence and empirical correctness – is a well-studied subfield within NLP.
Methods to measure it already exist.
The problem is adoption: outside this subfield, NLP research regularly introduces new models, datasets, and benchmarks without checking whether the model’s confidence scores are meaningful. We argue that this adoption gap is a major obstacle to trustworthy LLM evaluation. Miscalibration causes problems in two distinct areas: at deployment, where overconfident mistakes cause real harm, and inside the research pipeline, where methods like LLM-as-a-judge, synthetic data generation, and active learning rely on calibrated confidence without verifying it. Standard calibration metrics
only require two inputs per example: a confidence score and a correctness judgment. Most benchmarks in use today already provide both, meaning calibration can be reported immediately. For open-ended generation, however, defining these two inputs is still an open challenge. We argue that each NLP subfield should pair its main performance metric with a calibration score and call for treating calibration as an essential property of every model rather than a niche topic.
blocks.zh:
语言模型的校正——表达或隐含的信心与经验正确性之间的校正——是NLP内部一个研究良好的子领域.
衡量的方法已经存在。
问题在于采用:在这个子领域之外,NLP研究经常引入新的模型,数据集和基准,而不检查模型的置信分数是否有意义. 我们争辩说,这一收养差距是可信的LLM评价的主要障碍。 错误校准在两个不同的领域造成问题:在部署时,过度自信的错误会造成真正的伤害;在研究管道内,LLM-as-judge,合成数据生成等方法,以及主动学习依赖校准信任而不验证. 标准校准指标
每个例子只需要两个投入:信心分数和正确判断。 今天使用的大多数基准已经提供了两者,即校准可以立即报告。 然而,对于不限成员名额的一代来说,界定这两项投入仍然是一个公开的挑战。 我们主张,每个NLP子领域应当将其主要性能衡量标准与校准分数挂钩,并呼吁将校准视为每个模型的基本属性,而不是一个特殊专题。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Large language models (LLMs) have moved from research prototypes to tools used by millions of people every day, and this shift changes how we need to evaluate them. Earlier NLP systems were narrow, task-specific models whose outputs were
typically evaluated against a ground truth generated by domain experts.
In contrast, modern LLMs are general-purpose tools
that
can be applied to any task that takes text as input and produces text as output. Because of this versatility, millions of users now ask LLMs questions
about a large variety of topics, and the model’s confidence is the only indicator of the answer’s expected correctness.
Further, outputs are increasingly not read by humans at all, but fed directly into autonomous agents that act on them without supervision. A benchmark score is therefore no longer just the end of an experiment – it is the beginning of real-world deployment,
where outputs may have severe consequences.
blocks.zh:
大型语言模型(LLMs)已经从研究原型转向了每天数百万人使用的工具,这种转变改变了我们需要如何评价它们. 早先的NLP系统是狭窄的、针对具体任务的模型,其产出是:
通常根据域专家生成的地面真相进行评估。
相比之下,现代法学硕士是通用工具
那个
可用于任何将文本作为输入并生成文本作为输出的任务。 由于这种多元性,现在有数百万用户问LLMS问题
以及模型的信心是答案预期正确性的唯一指标。
此外,人类越来越不理解产出,而是直接将其输入在没有监督的情况下对其采取行动的自主代理人。 因此,基准得分不再仅仅是实验的结束,而是现实世界部署的开始,
产出可能产生严重后果。

blocks.en: Performance metrics, such as accuracy or F1, answer a single question: did the model produce the correct output? They do not answer the practical question that deployment requires: should we trust this output? Two models that are right 90% of the time are not interchangeable. A model whose confidence tracks its actual correctness is much more useful, because its 10% errors are flagged rather than looking identical to its 90% correct answers.
blocks.zh: 性能指标,如精度或F1,回答一个单一的问题:模型是否产生正确的输出? 它们不回答部署需要的实际问题:我们是否应该相信这一产出? 两个时间90%对的模型不能互换. 其信心追踪其实际正确性的模型更有用,因为其10%的错误被标出,而不是看上去与90%的正确答案完全相同。

blocks.en: The property that separates these two models is calibration – how well a model’s stated or implicit confidence matches whether it is actually correct. Calibration is not a new idea. It has been studied for decades in statistics and classification ( Brier, 1950 ; Guo et al., 2017 ) , and many recent NLP papers study it in LLMs ( Desai and Durrett, 2020 ; Jiang et al., 2021 ; Kadavath et al., 2022 ; Lin et al., 2022 ; Mielke et al., 2022 ; Tian et al., 2023 ; Ulmer et al., 2024 ; Ulmer et al., 2026 , inter alia ) . A recent survey ( Geng et al., 2024 ) organizes this literature. The methods are not the problem.
blocks.zh: 将这两个模型分开的属性是校准的 — — 一个模型所声明的或隐含的置信度如何与它是否实际正确相符。 校准不是一个新想法。 在统计和分类方面已经研究了几十年(Brier,1950年;Guo等人,2017年),最近许多NLP论文在LLMs(Desai and Durrett,2020年;Jiang等人,2021年;Kadavath等人,2022年;Lin等人,2022年;Mielke等人,2022年;Tian等人,2023年;Ulmer等人,2024年;Ulmer等人,2026年等等)中研究了这个问题. 最近的一项调查(Geng等人,2024年)组织了这一文献. 方法不是问题所在。

blocks.en: The problem is adoption. Outside the calibration subfield, NLP research often introduces new models, datasets, and benchmarks without measuring whether model confidence is meaningful. A machine translation paper reports BLEU ( Papineni et al., 2002 ) . A summarization paper reports ROUGE ( Lin, 2004 ) . An information extraction paper reports F1. A new benchmark publishes a leaderboard ranked only by accuracy. In each case, the question does the model know when it is wrong? remains unanswered.
blocks.zh: 问题在于收养。 在校准子领域之外,NLP研究经常引入新的模型,数据集,和基准,而不衡量模型置信度是否有意义. 一份机器翻译文件报告BLEU(Papineni等人,2002年)。 汇总论文报告ROUGE(林,2004). 资料提取文件报告F1. 一个新的基准只根据准确性来发布排行榜。 在每一种情况下,问题都是模型知道什么时候是错误的吗? 仍未答复。

blocks.en: This gap is clear at the highest level of model development. We reviewed the public technical reports and model cards for recent releases across major model families: GPT-5.5 ( OpenAI, 2026 ) , Claude Sonnet 4.6 ( Anthropic, 2026 ) , Gemini 3.5 Flash ( Google DeepMind, 2026 ) , DeepSeek V3.2 ( DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025 ) , Llama 3 ( Grattafiori et al., 2024 ) , Qwen3 ( Yang et al., 2025 ) , Gemma 3 ( Gemma Team et al., 2025 ) , GPT-OSS ( OpenAI et al., 2025 ) , and OLMo 3 ( Team Olmo et al., 2025 ) . All of them report results on dozens of capability and safety benchmarks, but none reports calibration. 1 1 1 This review is meant as an illustration, not as a complete survey. We may have missed isolated cases, but the pattern across widely used models is consistent. The GPT-4 technical report ( OpenAI et al., 2024 ) is a notable earlier exception that documents how reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) affects calibration, but later releases did not continue this practice.
blocks.zh: 这一差距在模型开发的最高一级是明显的。 我们审查了各大模范家庭最近发布的公共技术报告和示范卡:GPT-5.5(OpenAI,2026年),Claude Sonnet 4.6(Anthropic,2026年),双子座3.5 Flash(Google DeepMind,2026年),DeepSeek V3.2(DeepSeek-AI等人,2025年),Llama 3(Grattafiori等人,2024年), Quen3 (杨等人,2025年), Gemma. 3( Gemma ) Team等人,2025年),GPT-OSS(OpenAI等人,2025年),OLMo 3(Team Olmo等人,2025年). 他们都报告了数十项能力和安全基准的结果,但没有报告校准。 页:1 1 本审查旨在说明,而非完整的调查。 我们可能错过了孤立的案例,但广泛使用的模式的格局是一致的。 GPT-4技术报告(OpenAI等人,2024年)是早期一个显著的例外,记录了从人类反馈(RLHF)中强化学习如何影响校准,但后来的发布并没有继续这种做法.

blocks.en:
We argue that this adoption gap is a major obstacle to trustworthy LLM evaluation. Calibration is not a specialized topic for a single subfield; it is a basic property of every model and should be evaluated as such. After defining calibration for LLMs (§ 2 ), we discuss three main points:
1) Miscalibration causes problems in two places: at deployment, where overconfident errors cause concrete harm, and inside the research pipeline, where common practices (such as LLM-as-a-judge, synthetic data generation, and active learning) assume model confidence is calibrated without checking it (§ 3 ).
2) Existing calibration metrics need only two inputs per example: a confidence score and a correctness judgment. Most current benchmarks already provide both. Where metrics do not apply directly (such as open-ended generation), the challenge is defining these two inputs, not creating entirely new metrics (§ 4 ).
3) Closing this gap requires two steps that can happen in parallel: adopting community reporting standards for the tasks where metrics already work today and researching how to define confidence and correctness for open-ended generation (§ 5 ).
blocks.zh:
我们争辩说,这一收养差距是可信的LLM评价的主要障碍。 校准不是单个子领域的一个专门专题;它是每个模型的基本财产,应当作为这样的评价. 在为LLMs确定校准(§2)之后,我们讨论三个主要要点:
1) 误判在两个地方造成问题:在部署时,过度自信错误造成具体伤害;在研究管道内,常见做法(如LLM-as-judge,合成数据生成和主动学习)假定模型置信度被校准而不检查(§3).
2) 现有的校准度量度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度度 目前的大多数基准已经提供了两者。 如果衡量标准不直接适用(例如不限成员名额的一代),则面临的挑战是界定这两种投入,而不是创造全新的衡量标准(第4节)。
3) 弥合这一差距需要同时采取两个步骤:在衡量标准今天已经起作用的任务中采用社区报告标准,并研究如何为不限成员名额的一代确定信心和正确性(第5节)。

blocks.en: 2 Calibration for LLMs
blocks.zh: 2 法学硕士学位校准

blocks.en: A predictor is calibrated if, among the predictions it makes with confidence p p , a fraction p p are correct ( Guo et al., 2017 ) . This is a population-level property and is separate from accuracy: a model that always predicts with confidence 0.7 and is correct 70% of the time is perfectly calibrated, even though we do not know in advance which individual answers are right. Measuring calibration requires two pieces of information for each example: a confidence score and a judgment of whether the output is correct. The correctness judgment usually comes directly from the task. The confidence score is less straightforward, because LLMs express confidence in at least three ways.
blocks.zh: 预测器如果在它满怀信心的p的预测中,一个分数p是正确的(Guo等人,2017年)。 这是一个人口层面的属性,与准确性是分开的:一个总是充满信心地预测0.7并且正确70%时间的模型是完全校准的,尽管我们事先并不知道哪些个人答案是正确的. 测量校正需要每个例子的两条信息:信心分数和判断输出是否正确. 正确性判断通常直接来自任务. 信心分数不太直截了当,因为LLMs至少以三种方式表达信心.

blocks.en:
An autoregressive LLM defines a distribution over output sequences as p ⁡ ( y ∣ x ) = ∏ t = 1 T p ⁡ ( y t ∣ x , y < t ) , p(y\mid x)=\prod_{t=1}^{T}p(y_{t}\mid x,y_{<t}), where each factor is the probability the model assigns to token y t y_{t} at step t t .
The sequence probability, often length-normalized as p ​ ( y ∣ x ) 1 / T p(y\mid x)^{1/T} to compare outputs of different lengths, is the natural extension of classifier confidence to generation, and it is where early calibration studies of transformer-based models began ( Desai and Durrett, 2020 ; Jiang et al., 2021 ) . It is also the only confidence signal that exists by construction; verbalized confidence and behavioral cues must be elicited or interpreted. Even in simple multiple-choice QA, extracting this signal involves design choices (e.g., which tokens represent the answer or how to account for answer length) that affect the measured confidence ( Sanz-Guerrero et al., 2025 ; Sanz-Guerrero and von der Wense, 2025 ) .
blocks.zh:
自动回转 LLM 将输出序列上的分布定义为 p ⁡ (y ∣ x) = ∏ t = 1 T ⁡ (y t ∣ x, y < t), p (y\ mid x) =\ prod_{t= 1}^{ T}p (y_{ t}\ mid x, y_{< t)),其中每个因子是模式在 step t t 指定给 y t_{t 的概率.
序列概率,常以p(y ××××××××××××××××××××××(y\mid××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××××× 这也是通过构建而存在的唯一信心信号;必须引出或解释口头化的信心和行为提示。 即使在简单的多选择QA中,提取这个信号也涉及影响测量置信度的设计选择(例如,哪一个符号代表答案或如何计算答案长度)(Sanz-Guerrero等人,2025年;Sanz-Guerrero和von der Wense,2025年).

blocks.en: The model is prompted to state its confidence in words (e.g., “I am 80% sure”). Recent work shows that this signal can be elicited for any task and that for instruction-tuned models it is sometimes better calibrated than raw probabilities ( Lin et al., 2022 ; Tian et al., 2023 ) .
blocks.zh: 该模式旨在表明它对文字的信心(例如“我百分之八十肯定”)。 近期的研究表明,对于任何任务来说,都可以获得这种信号,对于经指导调整的模型来说,有时这种信号的校准比原始概率更好(Lin等人,2022年;Tian等人,2023年)。

blocks.en: Models also indicate confidence through behavior, such as hedging, refusing to answer, or expressing doubt. These are implicit signals that users actually read and interpret.
blocks.zh: 模型还通过行为表示信心,如套期保值,拒绝回答,或表示怀疑. 这些是用户实际阅读和解释的隐含信号.

blocks.en: Token and sequence probabilities, verbalized confidence, and behavioral signals are not interchangeable. A model can have well-calibrated token probabilities but poorly calibrated verbalized confidence, or the reverse ( Kadavath et al., 2022 ; Tian et al., 2023 ) . In deployment, users and downstream components (such as autonomous agents) only see the generated text, not the internal softmax probabilities. Verbalized and behavioral calibration are therefore what users actually rely on, while token-level calibration remains important for model analysis, training, and selective-prediction systems that have direct access to log-probabilities. Any evaluation of calibration should clearly state which of these signals is being tested.
blocks.zh: 托肯和顺序概率,口头化信心,以及行为信号不能互换. 一个模型可以有精准的符号概率,但精准的口头自信,或者相反(Kadavath等人,2022年;Tian等人,2023年). 在部署中,用户和下游组件(如自主代理)只看到生成的文本,而不是内部软轴概率. 因此,虚拟化和行为校准是用户实际依赖的,而符号级校准对于模型分析,培训和有选择的可直接访问日志概率的预测系统仍然很重要. 对校准的任何评价都应明确说明正在测试哪些信号。

blocks.en: A second important distinction ( Kendall and Gal, 2017 ) separates the sources of uncertainty. Aleatoric uncertainty is irreducible: it comes from ambiguity in the input itself, such as a question with multiple valid answers or under-specified context. Epistemic uncertainty is reducible: it reflects the model’s lack of knowledge, which could shrink with more training data or better retrieval. Standard calibration metrics treat both types the same, but the distinction matters in practice because each calls for a different response – abstention for aleatoric uncertainty and retrieval or further training for epistemic uncertainty.
blocks.zh: 第二个重要区别(Kendall and Gal, 2017)分离了不确定性的来源. 蓄水不确定性是不可减少的:它来自输入本身的模糊性,例如一个有多个有效答案或未充分说明上下文的问题. 增生不确定性是可以减少的:它反映了模型缺乏知识,这种知识可以随着更多的培训数据或更好的检索而收缩. 标准校准衡量标准对两种类型都一视同仁,但在实践中区别很重要,因为每种类型都要求不同的反应 — — 放弃了感官不确定性和检索或感官不确定性的进一步培训。

blocks.en: 3 Why Calibration Failures Matter
blocks.zh: 3 校准失败为何重要

blocks.en: Below, we discuss three settings where poor calibration causes problems, followed by an explanation of why miscalibration continues to grow.
blocks.zh: 下面我们讨论三种校准差造成问题的环境,然后解释校准差为什么继续增长.

blocks.en:
Users naturally adjust their trust based on how confident a model appears ( Steyvers et al., 2025 ) . People are likely to act on a wrong answer if it sounds confident, but will double-check a correct answer if the model sounds hesitant ( Kim et al., 2024 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ) .
For example, in legal applications, evaluations of leading LLMs show hallucinated case citations and fabricated court decisions delivered with complete confidence ( Dahl et al., 2024 ) .
In medical question answering, hallucinated clinical facts and incorrect drug dosages remain a frequent failure mode ( Kim et al., 2025 ) , and non-expert users cannot easily detect them. In both settings, the real danger is not just that the model makes mistakes, but that it gives no warning when it does. A wrong answer is far more dangerous when expressed with absolute certainty than when presented with appropriate doubt. The opposite behavior is not helpful either: a model that hedges on every single response provides no useful signal. Both cases are calibration failures.
blocks.zh:
用户自然根据模型的出现信心来调整其信任(Steyvers等人,2025年). 人们可能会对错误的答案采取行动,如果它听起来很自信,但如果模型听起来犹豫,则会重复检查正确的答案(Kim等人,2024年;Zhou等人,2024年)。
例如,在法律应用中,对主要有限责任公司的评价显示,对案件的引用产生幻觉,法院裁决完全可信(Dahl等人,2024年)。
在医学问题回答中,幻觉的临床事实和不正确的药物剂量仍然是常见的故障模式(Kim等人,2025年),非专家用户无法轻易发现. 在这两种情况下,真正的危险不仅仅是模型会犯错误,而是在模型发生错误时不发出警告. 如果用绝对的确定性表达错误的答案,比用适当的怀疑表达错误答案,危险得多。 反面的行为也无济于事:一个在每一个响应上进行套期的模型没有提供有用的信号. 这两个案例都是校准失败.

blocks.en:
When LLMs are chained together in agentic pipelines (e.g., planner, retriever, and executor), confidence is the signal that tells the system whether to take an action, ask for user input, or stop. If one component is miscalibrated, its overconfident mistakes propagate directly into subsequent steps ( El-Yaniv and Wiener, 2010 ) .
In automated systems, frontier models can take actions at very low probabilities ( Serrano et al., 2026 ) , and standard calibration metrics will not see them.
A similar problem happens inside reasoning models that generate step-by-step chains of thought. Mistakes build on each other: an overconfident error early in a reasoning trace often leads to an incorrect final response. Measuring calibration only on the final answer misses these internal mistakes entirely. Evaluation should therefore examine the calibration of the entire reasoning trace, not just the final output ( Yoon et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh:
当LLMs在代理管道(如规划器,检索器,以及执行器)中被连在一起时,信心是指示系统是采取行动,要求用户输入,还是停止的信号. 如果一个组件被错误校准,其过度自信的错误直接传播到后续步骤(El-Yaniv和Wiener,2010年)。
在自动化系统中,前沿模型可以在极低概率下采取行动(Serrano等人,2026年),标准校准度量衡不会看到它们.
一个类似的问题发生在产生逐级思维链的推理模型内部. 误差相互借鉴:推理追踪早期的过度自信错误往往导致错误的最终反应. 仅根据最后答案衡量校准完全忽略了这些内部错误。 因此,评价应审查整个推理跟踪的校准情况,而不仅仅是最后产出(Yoon等人,2025年)。

blocks.en: Miscalibration does not just cause problems during deployment; it also damages the research process itself. Several common practices in NLP assume that model confidence is meaningful and fail when it is not. First, LLM-as-a-judge evaluation uses one model to score the outputs of another. If the judge is miscalibrated, the resulting rankings, win rates, and reported improvements are biased. Second, synthetic data generation uses LLMs to create new training corpora. A miscalibrated generator produces confident errors that the next round of training then learns from. Finally, active learning, data filtering, and uncertainty-guided retrieval all select examples based on confidence scores, so miscalibrated confidence means selecting the wrong data points.
blocks.zh: 校准不当不仅在部署过程中造成问题,而且损害研究过程本身。 NLP中的一些常见做法认为模型信心是有意义的,如果不是,则失败. 首先,LLM-as-a-judge评价使用一种模式来评分另一种模式的产出。 如果法官的排名有误,结果的排名,胜率,以及报告的改进有偏差. 第二,合成数据生成使用LLMs来创建新的培训公司. 错误校准的生成器会产生信心错误,下一轮训练随后从中吸取教训. 最后,主动学习,数据过滤,和不确定性引导检索都根据置信分数选择实例,因此误判置信意味着选择错误的数据点.

blocks.en: 3.1 Increased Miscalibration: Post-Training Degrades Calibration
blocks.zh: 3.1 误差增加: 培训后降解校准

blocks.en:
Training optimizes what we measure, and we (generally) do not measure calibration. Base models are reasonably well calibrated on multiple-choice tasks. However, instruction tuning and RLHF hurt calibration, even when accuracy improves ( OpenAI et al., 2024 ) . Part of this issue comes from the conversational format itself: instruction-tuned models are significantly more confident in an answer when it is presented to them as their own output than when the same answer is provided by the user ( Sanz-Guerrero et al., 2026 ) . RLHF can also lead to increased rates of sycophancy ( Sharma et al., 2024 ) , where models adjust their confidence to agree with the user’s beliefs instead of reflecting whether they are actually right. Furthermore, Kalai et al. (2025) point out that most benchmarks give the same zero score to saying “I don’t know” as they do to an incorrect answer. As a result, guessing blindly is strictly preferable to abstaining, so current training and evaluation setups reward confident guessing, which directly promotes hallucinations.
When we optimize solely for headline accuracy, we end up damaging calibration because it remains unmeasured. Until we treat calibration as a first-class evaluation criterion, standard training pipelines will continue to degrade it.
blocks.zh:
训练使我们的衡量达到最佳,我们一般不测量校准。 基础模型在多项选择任务上有相当好的校准. 然而,指示调谐和RLHF损害校准,即使精度提高(OpenAI等人,2024年). 这个问题的一部分来自对话格式本身:当一个答案作为自己的产出提交给他们时,指导调制的模型比用户提供相同答案时(Sanz-Guerrero et al., 2026)要明显地更有信心. RLHF也可以导致节能率的提高(Sharma等人,2024年),其中模型调整其信心以认同用户的信念,而不是反映其是否实际正确. 此外,Kalai等人(2025年)指出,大多数基准给出的“我不知道”的分数与不正确的回答相同。 因此,盲猜严格来说胜于弃权,所以目前的训练和评价设置会奖励自信的猜测,这直接助长了幻觉.
当我们仅仅为了标题精度而优化时,我们最终会因为仍然没有测量而破坏校准. 在我们把校准作为一等评价标准之前,标准训练管道将继续降解.

blocks.en: 4 Current Metrics and Their Limits
blocks.zh: 4 当前的计量及其局限性

blocks.en: Below, we summarize standard calibration metrics and explain where each falls short for LLMs. All of these metrics require the same two inputs per example: a confidence score p ^ i \hat{p}_{i} and a correctness label y i y_{i} . The mathematical formulation of the metrics does not depend on whether the task is classification or generation. What changes across tasks is how easy or difficult it is to define these two inputs.
blocks.zh: 下面我们总结标准校准度量表,并解释每个校准度量表的不足之处。 所有这些衡量标准每个例子都需要相同的两个输入:一个信任分数p ^ i\ hat{p}_{i}和一个正确性标签y i y_{i}. 计量的数学公式并不取决于任务是分类还是生成. 不同任务的变化是界定这两种投入是多么容易或困难。

blocks.en:
ECE partitions predictions into M M confidence bins and reports the weighted average gap between bin accuracy and bin confidence: ECE = ∑ m = 1 M | B m | N ​ | acc ⁡ ( B m ) − conf ⁡ ( B m ) | , \mathrm{ECE}=\sum_{m=1}^{M}\frac{|B_{m}|}{N}\bigl|\,\mathrm{acc}(B_{m})-\mathrm{conf}(B_{m})\,\bigr|, where B m B_{m} is the set of predictions in bin m m and N N is the total number of predictions ( Pakdaman Naeini et al., 2015 ; Guo et al., 2017 ) .
The same bins give the reliability diagram , which plots bin accuracy against bin confidence: a perfectly calibrated model lies on the diagonal, points below it indicate overconfidence, and points above it indicate underconfidence.
Two limitations are especially important for LLMs. First, ECE estimates are bin-sensitive and statistically biased ( Kumar et al., 2019 ) , and the reported value depends on binning choices that are rarely justified.
Second, ECE assumes a single numerical confidence score for each prediction over a fixed set of classes. For open-ended generation, defining “the prediction” and “its confidence” is not straightforward.
blocks.zh:
欧洲经委会对M置信箱的预测,并报告bin准确度和bin置信度之间的加权平均差距: ECE = ∑ ∑ ∑ | | | | | ⁡(B m m | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ECE ECE }^{ }^{ }^{ }^{ }^{ }^{ |\ |\ |\ |\ |\ |\ |\ |\ |\ |\ |\ |\ |\ |\ |\ |\ } } } }
同样的垃圾箱给出了可靠性图,该图将垃圾箱的准确度与垃圾箱的置信度比对:一个完美校准的模型位于对角上,下面的点表示过度自信,上面的点表示不信任。
有两个限制对法学硕士特别重要。 首先,欧洲经委会的估计数是bin敏感和统计偏颇的(Kumar等人,2019年),报告的数值取决于极少有正当理由的binning选择。
第二,欧洲经委会假设,在一组固定的类别中,每项预测都有一个数值信任分。 对不限成员名额的一代来说,界定“预测”和“其信心”不是直截了当的。

blocks.en: For a binary outcome y ∈ { 0 , 1 } y\in\{0,1\} with predicted probability p ^ \hat{p} , the Brier score ( Brier, 1950 ) is the mean squared error over N N predictions: BS = 1 N ​ ∑ i = 1 N ( p ^ i − y i ) 2 \mathrm{BS}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}(\hat{p}_{i}-y_{i})^{2} Unlike ECE, which can be pushed toward zero simply by predicting the overall dataset accuracy, the Brier score is a proper scoring rule : it is minimized only when the predicted probabilities match the true empirical frequencies. However, like ECE, the Brier score assumes discrete outcomes. Applying it to free-form text requires simplifying each generated response into a binary correct-or-incorrect label, which leaves out important nuances in open-ended answers.

blocks.en: AUROC measures the probability that a randomly selected correct prediction receives a higher confidence score than a randomly selected incorrect one: AUROC = Pr ⁡ ( s ^ ​ ( x + ) > s ^ ​ ( x − ) ) , \mathrm{AUROC}=\Pr\bigl(\hat{s}(x^{+})>\hat{s}(x^{-})\bigr), where s ^ \hat{s} is the confidence score, x + x^{+} is a correctly classified input, and x − x^{-} is an incorrectly classified one. Related evaluation curves, e.g., the accuracy–rejection curve, measure how much accuracy improves when the model abstains from answering low-confidence predictions ( El-Yaniv and Wiener, 2010 ) . Because AUROC depends only on the ranking of confidence scores rather than their numerical values, a model that inflates all its confidences by the same amount keeps the same AUROC. Thus, AUROC measures ranking (how well confidence separates correct from incorrect answers) rather than calibration (whether the confidence numbers themselves are meaningful), which is less interpretable and less useful for deployment.
blocks.zh: AUROC 测量随机选择的正确预测得到比随机选择的不正确预测更高的置信分的概率: AUROC = Pr → (s ^ (x + )) = s → (x + ) ,\ mathrm → AUROC → Pr\bigl (\hat{s} (x^{+}) + + + + + ),其中 S ^\ → + + + + + + 是一个正确的分类输入, x + + + + + → 是一个错误的分类输入. 相关的评价曲线,如准确度–拒绝率曲线,当模型不回答低信心预测时,衡量准确度提高多少(El-Yaniv和Wiener,2010年). 因为AUROC只取决于置信分数的排名,而不是其数值,这个模型将它的所有置信度都以相同金额膨胀,保持了相同的AUROC. 因此,AUROC衡量排名(信心如何与错误的答案分开),而不是校准(信心数字本身是否有意义),这不易解释,对部署也不太有用。

blocks.en: For confidence, verbalized estimates can be elicited on almost any task and scored with the metrics above ( Lin et al., 2022 ; Tian et al., 2023 ; Xiong et al., 2024 ) , although they are sensitive to prompt phrasing, lack standardization across benchmarks, and mix two questions: whether the model internally knows it is uncertain, and whether it expresses that uncertainty accurately in words. Sequence probabilities are available whenever there is a single canonical target. For correctness, subfields already rely on established criteria: exact match in question answering, unit test pass rates in coding, or verified final answers in mathematics. Whenever this correctness check is binary (or can be made binary using a standard threshold), existing calibration metrics work directly. This applies to most benchmarks featured in the technical reports from Section 1 , which focus on multiple-choice, short-answer, math, and code generation tasks. Where standard metrics fail is open-ended generation: when many different answers are valid, there is no single target sequence whose probability we can measure, making both confidence and correctness harder to define. We turn to this open problem next.
blocks.zh: 对于信心而言,几乎任何任务都可以获得口头估计,并用上面的度量衡得分(Lin等人,2022年;Tian等人,2023年;Xiong等人,2024年),虽然对即时措辞很敏感,但缺乏跨基准的标准化,并混合了两个问题:模型内部是否知道其不确定性,以及它是否用文字准确表达这种不确定性. 只要有单一的犬科目标,就有序列概率。 对于正确性,子字段已经依赖既定的标准:在回答问题时精确匹配,在编码时单位测试通过率,或者在数学中核实最终答案. 当这种正确性检查是二进制(或者可以用标准阈值使二进制)时,现有的校准度量衡直接起作用. 这适用于第1节技术报告中的大多数基准,这些基准侧重于多重选择、短答、数学和代码生成任务。 在标准度量失败是无限的生成时:当许多不同的答案是有效的时,没有单一的目标序列,我们可以测量概率,这使得信心和正确性都难以定义. 我们接下来再谈这个公开的问题。

blocks.en: 5 Directions
blocks.zh: 5个方向

blocks.en: Below, we separate what can be done now from what still needs research, and close with one direction beyond calibration.
blocks.zh: 下面,我们把现在可以做的事 和仍然需要研究的事情分开, 紧接着一个超出校准的方向。

blocks.en:
Every subfield in NLP has its own standard metrics: BLEU and COMET in machine translation, ROUGE in summarization, F1 in information extraction, win rates in instruction following, and accuracy in QA. Each task should pair its primary metric with a calibration score that measures whether model confidence actually tracks performance. Doing this simply requires choosing a reasonable confidence signal, reusing the correctness criteria the subfield already relies on, and adding a column to the results table. Machine translation already shows this is possible: quality estimation predicts translation quality without a reference ( Specia et al., 2018 ) , serving as an effective confidence signal. Yet quality estimation scores are rarely reported alongside BLEU as an intrinsic property of the translation model.
The reason this is not standard practice is convention, not difficulty. The same convention explains why recent model releases (discussed in Section 1 ) report scores across dozens of capability benchmarks, but leave out calibration entirely.
blocks.zh:
NLP中每个子域都有自己的标准度量:机器翻译中的BLEU和COMET,汇总中的ROUGE,信息提取中的F1,以下指令中的中和率,以及QA中的准确度. 每项任务应将其主要指标与校准分配为一,以衡量模型信心是否实际跟踪性能。 这样做只需要选择一个合理的置信信号,重新使用子域已经依赖的正确性标准,并在结果表中增加一栏. 机器翻译已经表明这是可能的:质量估计预测翻译质量时没有参考(Specia等人,2018年),作为有效的信任信号. 然而,质量估计分数很少作为翻译模型的内在属性与BLEU一起报告。
这不是标准做法的原因是公约,而不是困难。 同一公约还解释了为何最近的模型发布(第1节讨论)报告数十项能力基准的得分,但完全不计算校准。

blocks.en: Community standards are the best way to drive change, and we propose two concrete changes. First, every benchmark result should include a calibration score alongside its main score, and major leaderboards should add a column for it. Second, reviewers should treat the absence of such reporting as a methodological gap, comparable to leaving out basic training settings. Kalai et al. (2025) suggest a related idea: change how benchmarks are scored so that being confidently wrong hurts a model’s score more than saying “I don’t know.” Instead of adding a new column, this changes what current leaderboards measure, and both ideas are compatible.
blocks.zh: 社区标准是推动变革的最佳途径,我们提出了两项具体的变革。 第一,每个基准结果都应包括校准分数和其主要分数,主要领导板应为其增加一栏。 第二,审查人员应将缺乏这种报告视为一种方法上的差距,相当于不提供基本培训的情况。 卡莱等人. (2025年)提出了一个相关的想法:改变基准的得分方式,让自信的错误伤害一个模型的分数,而不是说“我不知道 ” 。 与其添加新栏目,这可以改变当前领导板测量的,两个想法都是兼容的.

blocks.en:
Most modern LLM applications involve open-ended generation, where confidence and correctness are not yet clearly defined, and this is the area that still needs research.
Grouping generated responses by meaning rather than surface wording ( Kuhn et al., 2023 ) is a starting point. However, standardizing approaches and analyzing how they perform across tasks remains open. Crucially, this research should move forward in parallel with reporting norms on simpler tasks, rather than delaying them.
blocks.zh:
大多数现代LLM应用都涉及开放式的一代,其中信心和正确性还没有明确界定,而这正是仍然需要研究的领域.
按含义而不是表面措辞分组生成的答复(Kuhn等人,2023年)是一个起点。 然而,各种办法的标准化和分析如何在各项任务之间进行。 至关重要的是,这项研究应与关于较简单任务的报告规范平行进行,而不是拖延。

blocks.en: In practical applications, users interact directly with a model’s generated text, including any stated confidence or doubts. The NLP community should therefore treat verbalized confidence as an evaluation target in its own right, developing standardized prompt formats, consistent scoring methods, and analyses that distinguish between what a model internally knows and what it actually says. Ulmer et al. (2026) take this a step further, arguing that verbalized uncertainty should reflect natural human communication. Because users interpret model statements the same way they interpret human conversation, a model whose numerical probabilities are accurate but whose expression of uncertainty sounds unnatural might still mislead readers.
blocks.zh: 在实际应用中,用户与模型生成的文本直接互动,包括任何声明的信任或怀疑. 因此,NLP社区应该将口语化的信心作为自己的评价目标,制定标准化的即时格式,一致的评分方法,并进行分析,区分一个模型内部知道的内容和它实际所说的内容. Ulmer等人(2026年)对此更进一步,认为口头化的不确定性应反映人类的自然交流. 因为用户对模型语句的诠释方式与对人类对话的诠释方式相同,这个模型的数值概率是准确的,但其表达的不确定性听起来并不自然,仍然可能误导读者.

blocks.en: Calibration answers one fundamental question about trust: when should we believe an output? A second question is why : what evidence supports it? For LLMs, training data provides this evidence, and attribution methods aim to identify which training examples most influenced a particular output ( Koh and Liang, 2017 ; Grosse et al., 2023 ) . Calibration and attribution complement each other well: calibration gives users a score indicating how much to trust an answer, while attribution provides verifiable evidence showing whether a confident response is genuinely grounded in training data. While attribution methods are not yet as mature as calibration metrics, they face the exact same adoption challenge. Once these methods become practical, attribution should also be reported as a standard property of every model rather than treated as a niche experiment.
blocks.zh: 校准解答了一个关于信任的根本问题:我们何时应该相信产出? 第二个问题是,为什么:哪些证据可以证明这一点? 对于LLMS,培训数据提供了这种证据,归属方法旨在确定哪些培训实例对某一特定产出影响最大(Koh和Liang,2017年;Grosse等人,2023年)。 校准和归属是相辅相成的:校准给用户一个分数,表明对答案的信任程度,而归属则提供可核实的证据,表明自信的响应是否真正基于培训数据. 虽然归属方法还没有达到校准度量的成熟程度,但它们面临着完全相同的领养挑战. 一旦这些方法变得切实可行,归属也应作为每个模型的标准属性报告,而不是作为特殊实验处理。

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
As LLMs move from research to widespread use, our evaluation practices must change as well.
Practical methods to evaluate calibration already exist, but mainstream NLP research often overlooks them. This adoption gap creates risks in deployment when overconfident mistakes go unnoticed, and it undermines research pipelines that rely on uncalibrated models. For most benchmarks, the necessary calibration metrics are already available – all that is missing is the community standard to report them. For open-ended generation, defining appropriate metrics remains an important research challenge.
blocks.zh:
随着法学硕士从研究转向广泛使用,我们的评价做法也必须改变。
评估校准的实用方法已经存在,但主流NLP研究往往忽略了这些方法. 这种收养差距在过度自信的错误不被注意时造成了部署风险,并破坏了依赖未校准模型的研究管道。 对大多数基准来说,必要的校准指标已经存在 — — 所缺少的只是社区报告标准。 对于不限成员名额的一代来说,确定适当的衡量标准仍然是一个重要的研究挑战。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: This is a position paper without new empirical experiments; our arguments build on findings from existing literature. In addition, calibration for open-ended generation does not yet have a consensus definition. We focus our concrete reporting proposals on tasks where calibration metrics are already well established, while emphasizing that developing metrics for free-form generation remains an essential area for future research.
blocks.zh: 这是一份没有新的经验实验的立场文件;我们的论点以现有文献的结论为基础。 此外,对不限成员名额一代人的校准还没有达成共识的定义。 我们的具体报告建议侧重于已经建立校准指标的任务,同时强调,制定自由形式生成指标仍然是今后研究的一个重要领域。
